title: Are You Sure the Problem Is Pajamas, Sean Duffy?
text:
Well, well, well. If it isn’t my old nemesis, Sean Duffy, in the news again. Did something happen at the airports, Sean? Was it very bad? Would you go so far as to describe it as a serious problem? Worse, say, than people dressing casually at the airport, perhaps even in pajamas ? Because I would.

 Yes, it’s me, Pajamas.

 Now, I’m only a breathable, comfortable nighttime garment, but I think it is good when the planes aren’t afraid to go up and then come down again. To me, that is the most important thing that happens at an airport. Call me old-fashioned, but I think the planes should get to leave the ground . That’s just a superstition I have!

 A total ground stop. Planes everywhere, stuck on the tarmacs; spoonfuls of mashed bananas, unable to reach reluctant toddlers’ mouths. For hours, you say? Now, that sounds like a real airport problem. It would be a shame if you had alienated your old friend Travel Pajamas in a situation like this.

 I do not mean to question how much you know about aviation. I am just a simple set of sleep garments. My job is to help people sleep easily. I don’t know what your job is! Something where you get to appear on television a lot and nothing is your fault?

 In times of trouble, Mr. Rogers always told us to look for the helpers. Well, pajamas were there, helping. Pajamas swathed travel-weary limbs in a soft fabric embrace. Where were you? Saying on CNN that you “take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations”? That doesn’t sound like taking responsibility. But then again, I am just sleepwear. I am cozy with everyone, not just the industry I am meant to regulate .

 The fact that your reality-TV show (no, not The Real World , the other one) was called The Great American Road Trip and not Touring America Safely via Uninterrupted Air Travel should perhaps have signaled to us that all was not well.

 I know you love a scapegoat. I was your first. And now I am sure you will find someone to blame. Blame AI! Blame “systems”! Blame the “patriot” who installed the router! Say you don’t know what the problem was, but you will need $50 billion to fix it! That won’t fly, not unlike every plane on Friday night .

 I would suggest that this incident was someone’s chickens coming home to roost—or they would have been coming home to roost if there weren’t a ground stop. This was a case of chickens circling above the airport hoping for permission to land, then being stuck on the tarmac for hours.

 When you slandered me, all those months ago, and blamed me for everything that was wrong with air travel, I held my peace. I kept it buttoned. But now I am asking respectfully (I know respect means a lot to you) for my apology. Was the problem really that people were not dressing like it was 50 years ago, Sean? Was that really the problem?

 Thank you for your time. Good day! I will see you this evening, when I will do my best to make you as happy and comfortable as you have failed to make me.

 Sincerely,

 Pajamas
